guides.title: Calm down in 2 minutes
shortSteps: Dim the lights and reduce stimulation.
Hold with firm support and head supported.
When calm, lay back down gently.
guides.safetyNote: If you're feeling sleepy, put the baby in a safe place.

guides.title: Difficult night: keep low stimulation
shortSteps: No playing, no bright lights, no screens.
Do what's needed (feed/change) and lay back down.
If crying, use a simple and consistent routine.
guides.safetyNote: If you're feeling sleepy, put the baby in a safe place.

guides.title: 60s breathing for parents
shortSteps: Repeat 6 times. Only the next minute matters.
guides.safetyNote: If you're feeling sleepy, put the baby in a safe place.

guides.title: Transfer to the crib
shortSteps: Bring the baby close to the mattress slowly.
Firm hands: one on the torso, one supporting the head.
Touch the torso first, then the head.
Keep your hand there 10–20s, then slowly remove.
guides.safetyNote: If you're feeling sleepy, put the baby in a safe place.

bullets: If needed, pick up calmly and put back in crib when calmer.
If you're exhausted, ask for help. Safety first.

safetyChecklist.title: Safe sleep checklist (10s)
items: Clear crib: no pillows, loose blankets, 'nests', positioners or toys.
Same room, separate bed (share room, not bed).
Avoid overheating: light clothing, comfortable temperature.
safetyChecklist.warning: Avoid falling asleep with the baby on the sofa/armchair — this is one of the highest risk scenarios.

volumeSafetyMessage: Low volume and device away from the crib.
volumeHighWarning: If the indicator is in the high zone, consider lowering the volume.
disclaimer: This is practical and safe support. It doesn't guarantee sleep. If you have medical concerns, talk to a professional.
